messages:
alyssa: CI microbench ALERT: prefetch-metering delta +12% tokens/op on PR #2112 — crossed perf threshold.
sam: ugh, saw that. repro locally on avx-ci too? quick run shows similar numbers.
igor: I ran the perf harness, looks like batch path spent more time in kv_sampler::record() after the recent observability shim.
alyssa: exactly — this PR added a lightweight metering shim to count prefetches (instrumentation only). it was supposed to be noop.
diana: any flamegraphs or stacks? can you paste the hotspot?
sam: flamegraph snippet from the failing CI job:
```
  35%  runtime  kv_batcher::process
   22%   kv_sampler::record
    18%    instrumentation::meter_prefetch
     12%     atomic::fetch_add
```
mike: atomic noise suggests contention on the counter. were we using a global counter per worker thread?
igor: PR introduced a global PrefetchMeter singleton for telemetry aggregation to reduce logs; I think the atomic is shared across hot batchers.
alyssa: CI job uses many parallel microbench workers; atomics add up. local single-worker runs are quiet, multi-worker runs show the +12%.
perf-bot: perf-test: pr/2112 microbench-prefetch (linux-avx) — status: FAILED — delta +12.3% (threshold +5%)
diana: if it's only instrumentation, we should revert the shim or switch to per-thread counters with periodic aggregation.
sam: can we confirm bisect? candidate PRs: 2109 (kv_sampler refactor), 2112 (prefetch-metering), 2116 (batcher minor tweak). initial suspect is 2112.
igor: quick git bisect plan:
1) start at baseline commit before these PRs
2) run microbench parallel harness
3) narrow to change
I'll run a bisect CI job with a smaller matrix to save cloud credits.
alyssa: thanks. but if bisect confirms instrumentation, we should hotfix revert on release branch — this is blocking rollout.
mike: alternative quick mitigation: make PrefetchMeter use thread-local counters (no atomics under fast path) and aggregate on flush. cheap patch.
sam: I prototyped thread-local counters earlier, perf improved to +1.8% (within noise). patch looks small.
igor: can you open a follow-up PR with thread-local approach and mark it as hotfix? we'll queue for post-merge revert if needed.
sam: PR #2120 created: "prefetch: threadlocal meter to avoid atomic contention" — link: https://git.redwood/pr/2120
perf-bot: perf-test: pr/2120 microbench-prefetch (linux-avx, parallel=8) — queued
alyssa: also schedule a revert PR for 2112 as insurance (label: rollback-ready).
diana: reverts are messy. prefer the minimal hotfix approach if tests show it's green.
perf-bot: perf-test: pr/2120 finished — delta +0.9% (within threshold) — status: PASS
alyssa: great news. can we merge 2120 into main and then roll 2112? sequence: merge 2120 (hotfix) -> merge 2112 (functionality) -> remove revert for safety.
igor: agree. I'll prepare a post-merge checklist: monitor kv_sampler atomics via infra metrics, add a small microbench (parallel stress) to our CI goldens to catch this.
mike: also add a note to release playbook: avoid global atomics on hot paths; prefer thread-local aggregation.
sam: one follow-up: add a smoke-run to PR checks that spins up parallel harness w/ concurrency=8 for 30s to catch atomic-contention noise.
alyssa: filing infra tickets and adding to PR template. thanks everyone :thumbsup
__notes: thread about CI microbench regression caused by instrumentation atomic contention; includes bisect plan, hotfix PR, perf-bot updates, and rollout decision.
